brief: Weekly Barclays portfolio-manager digest spanning three new pieces plus abstracts of the week's other research. Neo-cloud credit (CoreWeave) has repriced sharply on doubts about debt-funded AI infrastructure, amplified by hedge-fund de-risking and press reports; credit relief has not passed through to equities, so options and equity pricing still show bearish neo-cloud positioning, even though Barclays judges the supply/demand and take-or-pay fundamentals more resilient than price action implies. Data-center-supply names (semis, electronic/electrical equipment) de-rated most since Sep 30 while software and large-cap value re-rated higher. A new systematic framework converts US macro data into six regime probabilities to drive European sector allocation; as of end-September expansion/transition dominate, keeping the model pro-cyclical (overweight Industrials and Technology) though cyclical tilt has eased from its 2025 peak as defensive exposure is added back. Separately, Barclays maps ~80 companies across the battery value chain as chemistries diverge beyond EVs. Elsewhere: rising oil is pressuring France/Italy fiscal risk and reviving bond safe-haven demand against hit equities, Asia hedge funds keep de-risking into bounces, and AI credit dispersion is rising as curves steepen.
